question: How does the author identify himself in the opening of his second epistle, and unto whom is it addressed?
opt1: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth
opt2: The apostle of the circumcision unto the dispersed churches of Galatia and Cappadocia
opt3: The servant of Jesus Christ unto the synagogue elders throughout Alexandria and Judea
opt4: The prisoner of the Lord unto the saints established in the municipal assemblies of Rome
correct: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth
explanation: John designates himself with pastoral dignity as 'the elder', writing with warm affection to the elect lady and her children, united together in divine truth. 2 John 1:1 (KJV) - "The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;"

question: What permanent spiritual foundation motivates the apostle's love for the elect lady and her household?
opt1: For the sake of common commercial enterprises and trade alliances established across Asia
opt2: For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever
opt3: For the sake of ancient patriarchal genealogies preserved in the temple archives
opt4: For the sake of reciprocal political patronage during seasons of civic scrutiny
correct: For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever
explanation: Christian love is rooted not in transient human emotion or worldly advantage, but in the indwelling, eternal truth of God that abides forever within believers. 2 John 1:2 (KJV) - "For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever."

question: What threefold divine blessing does John pronounce upon the recipients from the Father and the Son?
opt1: Honor, wealth, and authority, from the celestial thrones and planetary constellations, in power and majesty
opt2: Prosperity, health, and dominion, from the angelic hierarchy of heaven, in wisdom and strength
opt3: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love
opt4: Favor, tribute, and victory, from the earthly rulers and magistrates of Asia, in civic peace
correct: Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love
explanation: The apostolic salutation invokes grace, mercy, and peace rooted firmly in the divine relationship of the Father and His Son, operating within the sphere of truth and love. 2 John 1:3 (KJV) - "Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love."

question: What specific discovery regarding the elect lady's children caused the apostle John to rejoice greatly?
opt1: That they had acquired prominent municipal magistracies in the civic forums of Ephesus
opt2: That they had amassed substantial fortunes to construct monumental sanctuaries
opt3: That they had authored innovative philosophical treatises praised by Greek academies
opt4: That I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father
correct: That I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father
explanation: John rejoices not in worldly success or social prestige, but in witnessing the children of the elect lady actively ordering their lives in obedience to divine truth. 2 John 1:4 (KJV) - "I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father."

question: What fundamental commandment from the beginning does John emphasize, and how does he define authentic biblical love?
opt1: That we love one another: and this is love, that we walk after his commandments
opt2: That we enforce ritual fasts: and this is love, that we observe monastic solitude
opt3: That we debate philosophical riddles: and this is love, that we outwit secular adversaries
opt4: That we accumulate charitable endowments: and this is love, that we purchase civic honors
correct: That we love one another: and this is love, that we walk after his commandments
explanation: The apostolic commandment is not an innovative novelty but the ancient command to love one another, practically expressed through steadfast obedience to God's commandments. 2 John 1:5-6 (KJV) - "And now I beseech thee, lady, not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another. And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it."

question: How does John describe the deceptive false teachers who have gone out into the world, and what serious title does he assign to them?
opt1: Who refuse to pay municipal taxes to Caesar. This is a seditious rebel and an outlaw
opt2: Who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist
opt3: Who neglect the ceremonial washings of the hands. This is an ignorant proselyte and a novice
opt4: Who teach that believers may engage in maritime trade. This is a worldly merchant and an idolater
correct: Who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist
explanation: The critical mark of the antichrist deceiver is the denial of the true incarnation of Jesus Christ in actual human flesh. 2 John 1:7 (KJV) - "For many deceivers are entered into the world, who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist."

question: What earnest warning does John deliver to believers concerning their spiritual vigilance and eternal reward?
opt1: Look to the stars, that ye may calculate the exact chronology of earthly empires
opt2: Look to the magistrates, that ye may secure legal exemptions from public taxation
opt3: Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward
opt4: Look to the marketplace, that ye may guard your commercial investments against loss
correct: Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward
explanation: Believers are summoned to personal vigilance lest deception rob them of the fruit of apostolic labor, striving instead to attain a full heavenly reward. 2 John 1:8 (KJV) - "Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward."

question: What decisive spiritual truth does John pronounce regarding anyone who transgresses and fails to abide in the doctrine of Christ?
opt1: Whosoever transgresseth merely requires additional philosophical tutoring in Greek logic
opt2: Whosoever abideth not in the doctrine of Christ may still possess the Father through natural religion
opt3: Whosoever transgresseth incurs temporary ecclesiastical probation without affecting fellowship with God
opt4: Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son
correct: Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son
explanation: Departing from the revealed apostolic doctrine concerning Christ severs communion with God, whereas abiding in Christ's doctrine secures vital fellowship with both the Father and the Son. 2 John 1:9 (KJV) - "Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son."

question: What strict pastoral prohibition does John give regarding hospitality toward itinerant teachers who deny the doctrine of Christ?
opt1: Receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed: for he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds
opt2: Welcome him into your assembly, and grant him the pulpit to debate his alternative opinions
opt3: Provide him with financial stipends and letters of commendation to other Christian assemblies
opt4: Invite him to dine at your table while privately ignoring his heretical christological errors
correct: Receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed: for he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds
explanation: Extending hospitality or welcoming greetings to false teachers who subvert the gospel makes one a moral accomplice and co-participant in their destructive, evil deeds. 2 John 1:10-11 (KJV) - "If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed: For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds."

question: Why did John refrain from writing further with paper and ink, and who conveys concluding fraternal greetings to the elect lady?
opt1: Because ink and parchment were scarce throughout Asia Minor. The Roman garrison elders greet thee
opt2: But I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full. The children of thy elect sister greet thee
opt3: Because an imperial ban prohibited all correspondence between assemblies. The synagogue rulers greet thee
opt4: Because he intended to compose an extensive legal brief for the provincial governor. The trade guild greets thee
correct: But I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full. The children of thy elect sister greet thee
explanation: John preferred personal, face-to-face communion over written correspondence to maximize spiritual joy, concluding with affectionate greetings from the children of the lady's elect sister church. 2 John 1:12-13 (KJV) - "Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and ink: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full. The children of thy elect sister greet thee. Amen."
